title: Stepped fallback & client feature-flag playbook for legacy stream deprecation
creator: Priya Nair
description: Purpose: define a conservative, low-risk migration playbook that combines server-side compatibility shims, client feature flags, and stepped fallback rules to retire the legacy /chatstream endpoints without causing customer outages. Scope: per-tenant grace windows, SDK compatibility support, runtime aliasing and a short-lived compat header for customers who cannot migrate immediately. Out of scope: redesign of client SDKs; full removal of server-side SHIM until 2026-Q3.
acceptance_criteria: A1: Compatibility shim in API gateway accepts X-Compat-Mode header and correctly routes to legacy handler for flagged tenants
A2: Feature-flag system supports per-org enable/disable with rollout percentages and audit logging
A3: Console shows per-tenant migration status and exposes opt-in/opt-out for the compat shim
A4: SDK patch (python/javascript) is published with wired-in 1-click migration helper and an experimental environment variable ENABLE_NEW_STREAM_API
A5: Monitoring dashboard surfaces migration progress and shows >=99.5% success rate for requests routed to new endpoints during canary
A6: Communication templates for email/console banner recorded, legal reviewed, and scheduled per the timeline below
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (Prep, 4 weeks): Build compat shim and feature-flag hooks. Create console UI mockups and approval from legal/CS.
Phase 1 (Internal canary, 1 week): Flip flag for internal tenants and Redwood dev org. Validate latency/cost regressions and failure modes.
Phase 2 (Partner canary, 2 weeks): Invite 10 high-touch customers to opt-in via account manager. Monitor errors/latency/CS tickets daily.
Phase 3 (Gradual public, 6 weeks): Enable for 10% of eligible orgs, increase by 10% weekly with rollback guardrails. Use opt-in header for remaining orgs.

Phase 4 (Grace window & enforcement, 12 weeks after Phase 3 start): Send automated notices, then begin automatic re-routing off the compat shim for orgs that have not migrated (with soft-fail telemetry for first 48h).
Phase 5 (Removal window, target Q3 2026): Deprecation flag will be removed after comprehensive success criteria met and exec sign-off.
migration_guidance: Recommended client change: replace /chatstream with /unified/stream; map the stream init schema field 'conversation_id' -> 'session_id' as noted in the API diff doc.
Temporary mitigation: clients can send header 'X-Compat-Mode: legacy-v1' to keep traffic on legacy handler during their migration window.
SDK changes: publish python v1.3.2 and js v2.7.0 which provide a 'migrate_stream()' helper and emit migration telemetry events visible in Console.
Edge cases: streaming tokenization differences for long prompts must be handled by new SDK flag 'preserve_kv_cache=true' — servers will accept both encodings during the grace window.
Sample migration timeline for a mid-size customer: 2 developer-days to update SDK, 1 day of integration testing, 1 week of canary on staging, 1 week of production validation.
monitoring_and_metrics: Dashboard: Console -> Migrations -> Legacy Stream shows requests_by_endpoint, error_rate, p95_latency, percent_using_compat_header over time
SLO targets while migrating: p95 latency <= baseline + 25ms; error_rate <= baseline + 0.5%
Runbooks: automated rollback if new-endpoint error_rate > 1% for 10 minutes or if p95 latency increases by >20% for more than 15 minutes
Telemetry: SDK emits migration.step events; per-tenant migration timestamp stored in metadata table for audit
communications: Week 0: Internal announcement in #platform-announce and internal doc at https://confluence.redwood.ai/pm/migrations/legacy-stream-playbook
Week 2: Partner outreach template and account manager checklist (doc link included in linked_artifacts)
Week 4: Public deprecation notice via Console banner, changelog, and targeted emails to admins of affected orgs
Pre-removal: 30/14/7 day automated notices plus in-console migration checklist with one-click SDK update guidance

Agree on final canary org list (action: Solutions Eng and CSM to propose 10 orgs by 2026-02-22)
